newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to raise minimum wage with bonus - report.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to raise minimum wage with bonus - report.

text.p: Venezuelan Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said the government would increase the minimum wage with a temporary "bridging bonus" on May 1 if Congress had not yet finished discussions of pending Labor Law reforms, leading daily El Nacional reported.
"May 1 is the traditional date for making such announcements," Petkoff said.

No final decision has yet been made on the size of the increase, although government officials have said the hike will be to between 62,000 and 75,000 bolivars ($129-157) per month from the current 53,000 bolivar level.

The minimum wage increase was to have followed congressional approval of Labor Law reforms. Raising the wage before the reforms are approved is expected to further slow potentially protracted discussions, government officials have said.
The reforms form part of a ground-breaking series of changes aimed at freeing-up Venezuela's rigid labor markets and revamping its crumbling social security system.
